audit_findings.title: Post-TEGNA interest burden is absent from the FY2025 owner-earnings claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $5.411 billion, from $6.333 billion at December 31, 2025 to $11.744 billion at June 30, 2026; interest expense increased $93 million year over year in Q2 and $115 million for the first six months, equal to 16.4% and 20.2% of the $568.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE anchor retains pre-acquisition interest expense while the valuation represents the post-acquisition company and does not deduct debt in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Under this agreement, a syndicate of financial institutions committed to provide up to $ 5.725 billion in debt financing to support the Merger, the refinancing of certain TEGNA obligations, and related transactions.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future cost. The filed post-closing results show a materially higher interest burden, while the DCF capitalizes FY2025 OE indefinitely. Because debt is not separately deducted, interest must be measured on the same post-closing perimeter as operating earnings. TEGNA's earnings partly offset this burden, so the net correction cannot be inferred from interest alone.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE from a single post-closing perimeter using full-year pro-forma TEGNA operations, the complete acquisition-financing interest and fee burden, required divestitures, integration costs and the injunction's effect; rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated VIE and NCI cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filing reports $538 million of VIE assets, $489 million of VIE liabilities and a $26 million 2025 net loss attributable to NCI, but does not allocate OE adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Starting with income attributable to Nexstar while applying consolidated depreciation, capital spending and other cash-flow adjustments can assign cash flows from VIE or NCI claims to Nexstar common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of our deemed controlling financial interests in the consolidated VIEs in accordance with U.S. GAAP, we consolidate the financial position, results of operations and cash flows of these VIEs as if they were wholly owned entities.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting bases are demonstrably different, but the resulting valuation error is unresolved. Nexstar states that it receives substantially all available VIE cash after operating costs and debt service, so legal ownership alone does not establish the parent economic share. Without entity-level depreciation, capital spending and working-capital allocations, neither direction nor materiality can be established.
audit_findings.action: Produce an entity-by-entity FY2025 OE reconciliation allocating every adjustment among Nexstar common equity, redeemable NCI, other NCI and consolidated VIE owners, including cash-transfer rights and VIE debt service; rerun if the parent OE changes.

audit_findings.title: TV Food Network may be capitalized twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $137 million of FY2025 distributions, $102 million of equity-method income, a $381 million impairment and a separate $327 million bridge addition; the distribution alone equals 24.1% of the $568.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: TV Food Network income or distributions retained in OE are capitalized through the DCF while the stake is also added in the equity bridge; retaining the impairment without adding it back would distort OE downward.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, we received cash distributions from TV Food Network totaling $137 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Double capitalization is not proven because the complete OE reconciliation is absent, but its possible scale is clearly material. The $137 million distribution alone is nearly one-quarter of anchor OE. The $381 million noncash impairment creates a potentially large offsetting distortion if treated inconsistently, so the net direction is mixed until the reconciliation is traced.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $102 million equity-method income, $137 million distribution, $69 million basis-difference amortization and $381 million impairment through FY2025 OE. Either purge all stake-related earnings and distributions and retain the $327 million bridge value, or capitalize the cash flows and remove the bridge addition, then rerun.

audit_findings.title: The CW minority owners hold a cash put ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $110 million estimated redemption value, or $3.46 per diluted share; deducting it reduces base value from $268.53 to approximately $265.07 and the 30%-MOS buy-below price from $187.97 to approximately $185.55, still $8.72 above the $176.83 market price
audit_findings.mechanism: The redeemable NCI is a cash claim ahead of common equity that should be deducted in the bridge unless its full economic cost is already removed from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the operating agreement governing The CW, Nexstar has a call right to acquire the noncontrolling ownership interests in The CW that is exercisable during a certain period each year, and each noncontrolling owner has a put right to sell its ownership interest in The CW to Nexstar beginning in June 2026, subject to Nexstar’s one year deferral right, for cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated by the filed $110 million redemption estimate and the absence of a deduction. One holder exercised its put on August 4, 2026. Nevertheless, the filed amount is only about 1.3% of base equity value and, considered alone, does not change the valuation conclusion after the stated margin of safety.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the exercised percentage, deferral election and settlement date, then deduct the full remaining redemption claim from the bridge or document an equivalent OE adjustment; no scenario-input change is required.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved Tribune tax exposure could consume common-equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: Potential $439 million computed from $225 million estimated tax plus $73 million proposed penalty plus $295 million after-tax interest through June 30, 2026, less $154 million of prior tax payments; approximately $13.82 per share and 5.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse appellate outcome creates a cash claim that would be deducted from the equity bridge and may also reduce tax basis and future after-tax OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Nexstar estimates that the federal and state income taxes would be approximately $ 225 million before interest and penalties.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a contingent exposure, not a demonstrated liability: the Tax Court previously found no deficiency or penalty, and the IRS appeal remained pending in the latest filing. However, the computed adverse-case exposure is close to the roughly $505 million bridge deduction that would erase the valuation's buy-below advantage at the quoted price, before considering additional basis effects. It is therefore reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Seventh Circuit disposition and docket status as of September 5, 2026; update interest through the valuation date and quantify penalties, the $154 million offset, basis reductions, indemnification and any tax benefit, then rerun the bridge for the supportable expected cash exposure.

audit_findings.title: Pension funding cost may not match the accounting credit retained in earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 pension credit of $30 million plus $19 million of employer contributions implies a potential $49 million OE mismatch if neither adjustment was made, equal to 8.6% of the $568.2 million anchor; filed legacy underfunding was $154 million, comprising $117 million of qualified-plan underfunding and $37 million of unfunded supplemental obligations
audit_findings.mechanism: Accounting pension credit increases earnings without current cash generation, while actual or normalized funding reduces OE; alternatively, an unfunded economic liability belongs in the bridge, without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: The qualified retirement plans also had $1.4 billion in total net assets available, or underfunded by approximately $117 million, to pay benefits to participants enrolled in the plans as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The pension amounts are filed and potentially material, but whether the $568.2 million anchor already removes the credit or captures contributions is unresolved. If it retains the $30 million credit and omits $19 million of cash funding, the recurring-anchor effect is large enough to threaten the buy conclusion. A bridge-only deduction of the $154 million legacy deficit would be smaller and would not by itself reverse the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $30 million credit, $19 million contributions and pension-related cash-flow-statement movements to FY2025 OE; update for the acquired TEGNA plan and the filed $39 million 2026 contribution expectation; use normalized cash funding in OE or deduct the economic deficit in the bridge, but not both, and rerun.
